Look at the block reached only by the true arm of the branch that tests
`all(uv < 0.5))` (source line 8). The source computes the level-of-detail value
unconditionally, before that branch. In both DXC panes below, the compiled IR places the LOD
calculation itself inside that conditionally-reached block instead -- after the branch, not
before it -- even though nothing about its inputs depends on the branch condition. That is the
illegal code motion the issue reports: the LOD calculation has been sunk into non-uniform
control flow. The Clang pane cannot corroborate or refute this: it rejects the shader earlier,
at Sema, because its HLSL front end does not yet recognise `InterlockedMin` as a free function.
